title: Clinical and MRI Characteristics of Delayed Onset Muscle Soreness (DOMS) of the Shoulder Rotator Muscles Induced by Eccentric Exercise: An Exploratory Prospective Experimental Study
official: Clinical and MRI Characteristics of Delayed Onset Muscle Soreness (DOMS) of the Shoulder Rotator Muscles Induced by Eccentric Exercise: An Exploratory Prospective Experimental Study
summary: The purpose of this study is to characterize the clinical and radiological manifestations of delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS) experimentally induced by an isokinetic eccentric contraction protocol targeting the shoulder rotator muscles in asymptomatic athletic subjects.
conditions: Delayed Onset Muscle Soreness Experimentally Induced
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Male subjects aged 18 to 45,
* No hormone therapy for the transgender population,
* Asymptomatic dominant shoulder,
* Athletes who have been performing upper-body strength training at least once a week for the past 3 months,
* Patients with no symptoms or history of: humeral, clavicular, or scapular fractures; glenohumeral, acromioclavicular, or sternoclavicular dislocations; shoulder surgery within the past 6 months; calcification; inflammatory arthritis; and/or tendon disorders,
* Enrollment in a social security program,
* Provision of information to the patient and obtaining the patient's free and informed consent.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Shoulder pain or history of shoulder pain
* Cognitive impairments deemed moderate to severe by the investigator Cardiac conditions that contraindicate maximal exertion
* Language barriers preventing participation in a rehabilitation program or the completion of a reliable assessment
* Persons under legal guardianship, conservatorship, or other legal protection
* Refusal to participate
